name: New on the Timetable!

pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.label: Pick a skill
pick.heading: Pick a skill and make it a school subject
lead: School taught you the dates of battles and how to work out the area of a triangle. Nobody taught you how to do your tax return, cook something that isn’t pasta, or survive the family group chat.

Choose a skill that schools ignore and turn it into a proper subject, with lessons, a teacher and a test. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The stranger, the better*, as long as you can say why children need it.
pick.note: I’m not asking you to write a curriculum. Some subjects will sound sensible and some will sound like a sitcom. Both are welcome.

rows: Which skill are you putting on the timetable?
What goes wrong in adult life without it?
What happens in the room? Who talks, who practises, what’s on the board?
A teacher, a guest, an app, someone’s grandmother?
An exam, a performance, a real-life task, something completely mad?
How I’d sell it to parents:
What would make a sceptical parent say yes?

values.subject: Folding a fitted sheet
values.why: Because no adult in history has ever done it properly. We all just roll it into a ball and hide it at the back of the cupboard, and the shame stays with us for life.
values.lesson: Pupils work in pairs, one sheet between two, while the teacher demonstrates very slowly, like someone defusing a bomb. The last ten minutes are free folding, with relaxing music.
values.teacher: Someone who has worked in a hotel for thirty years and has seen things.
values.test: A fitted sheet, a timer and the head teacher watching. Anything that goes into a drawer without falling open is a pass.
values.sell: Every child brings home a perfectly folded sheet at the end of term. Parents will cry.

yours.label: Your subject
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your subject in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which subject makes the timetable?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their subject in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
